content.title: About
content.content: Broccoli is an edible vegetable from the cruciferous family, originally from the Mediterranean region. Fresh florets are rich in vitamins, minerals, and fiber. When cooked with added fat (oil, butter) the bright color and flavor are enhanced.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Broccoli is sometimes called “little cabbage” because its florets resemble tiny heads.
It contains glucoraphanin, a compound that supports the body’s detoxification processes.
Ancient Romans used broccoli as a medicinal remedy for stomach ailments.
Short cooking methods (steaming, blanching) preserve the most nutrients.
In the United States broccoli is part of the “five‑a‑day” vegetable recommendation.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: One cup of cooked broccoli provides over 100 % of the daily vitamin C requirement, supporting immunity and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Source of folate
items.content: Folate is needed for cell division and is especially important during pregnancy.

items.title: Fiber and antioxidants
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, while antioxidants (lutein, zeaxanthin) protect eye health.

items.title: Beneficial fats when oil is added
items.content: Added fat helps absorb the fat‑soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) present in broccoli.

items.title: Gas and bloating
items.content: Broccoli contains raffinose, which can cause gas in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Interaction with anticoagulants
items.content: High vitamin K content may reduce the effectiveness of blood‑thinning medications.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Rarely, some people may be allergic to cruciferous vegetables.

items.title: Nutrient loss with prolonged boiling
items.content: Extended boiling leaches water‑soluble vitamins, so brief cooking is preferred.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Broccoli can be eaten raw in salads, steamed, blanched, sautéed with a small amount of oil, or added to soups and stews. When sautéing with oil, add garlic, pepper, or other spices to boost flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fresh broccoli in the refrigerator in a perforated bag or container, where it stays crisp for up to 5 days. Cooked broccoli should be kept in an airtight container in the fridge and consumed within 3 days.

content.title: About
content.content: Energy drink is a non‑alcoholic beverage enriched with caffeine, taurine, B‑vitamins and sugar or its substitutes. It is intended to boost alertness, improve concentration and temporarily increase physical endurance.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first commercial energy drink appeared in Japan in the 1960s under the brand “Lipovitan”.
A typical energy drink (80‑100 mg caffeine) contains roughly the same amount of caffeine as a strong cup of coffee.
Taurine, often added to these drinks, occurs naturally in meat and fish and helps regulate electrolyte balance.
Many countries restrict the sale of energy drinks to minors by law.
Some brands use natural extracts of guarana or ginseng to enhance the effect.

items.title: Increased alertness
items.content: Caffeine stimulates the central nervous system, improving attention and reaction time.

items.title: Energy replenishment
items.content: Sugar and glucose polymers quickly restore muscle glycogen, which can be useful during intense workouts.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B1, B2, B3, B6 and B12 support carbohydrate metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Electrolyte balance
items.content: Some formulas contain sodium and potassium, helping to prevent dehydration.

items.title: Mood enhancement
items.content: Caffeine raises dopamine levels, which may temporarily improve mood.

items.title: Excessive caffeine intake
items.content: High doses can cause anxiety, insomnia, rapid heartbeat and increased blood pressure.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Regular consumption of high‑sugar drinks raises the risk of tooth decay and obesity.

items.title: Interaction with alcohol
items.content: Mixing energy drinks with alcohol can mask intoxication, increasing the risk of overexertion.

items.title: Not recommended for children and pregnant women
items.content: Due to high caffeine and stimulant levels, these drinks are not advised for children, adolescents, pregnant or nursing women.

items.title: Cardiovascular concerns
items.content: People with heart conditions should limit or avoid energy drinks.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Energy drinks are usually consumed cold, straight from the can. A typical serving is 250‑350 ml (one can) within 1‑2 hours. Do not exceed 2‑3 servings per day and avoid combining with other caffeine sources.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the drink in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep it refrigerated and consume within 24 hours.

content.title: About
content.content: Enfamil AR is a ready‑to‑feed infant formula designed for children with increased energy and nutrient needs, such as those experiencing poor growth, excessive weight loss, or higher caloric requirements. It provides a blend of proteins, fats, carbohydrates, vitamins, minerals, and added DHA and ARA to support brain and eye development.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Enfamil AR is produced by Mead Johnson, a leading global manufacturer of pediatric nutrition.
The formula is fortified with the probiotic L. reuteri, which helps maintain a healthy gut microbiome.
It contains partially hydrolyzed casein to ease digestion for infants with sensitive stomachs.
The ready‑to‑feed format eliminates the need for preparation, making it convenient for travel and night feedings.
Enfamil AR meets WHO recommendations for infant formula composition for children over 6 months.

items.title: Supports growth and weight gain
items.content: High caloric density (≈ 22 kcal/oz) and balanced protein, fat, and carbohydrate levels help infants who need accelerated weight gain.

items.title: Brain and eye development
items.content: Added DHA and ARA contribute to neural development, visual acuity, and cognitive function.

items.title: Gut health
items.content: The probiotic L. reuteri promotes a balanced intestinal flora, reducing the risk of diarrhea and constipation.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Vitamins A, C, D and zinc support normal immune system function.

items.title: Easy digestion
items.content: Partially hydrolyzed casein reduces digestive load, lowering the chance of allergic reactions.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Infants with confirmed cow‑milk protein allergy or lactose intolerance should use a hypoallergenic formula.

items.title: Excess calorie intake
items.content: Without medical guidance, over‑feeding may lead to unwanted weight gain.

items.title: Improper storage
items.content: After opening, the formula must be refrigerated and used within 48 hours to prevent bacterial growth.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: The formula contains lactose; infants with lactose intolerance require a lactose‑free alternative.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Prepare a clean bottle or feeding cup, open the package, measure the recommended amount (typically 30 ml ≈ 1 oz) and feed immediately. Do not heat in a microwave; warm the bottle in warm water to body temperature.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened containers in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Once opened, keep refrigerated and use within 48 hours. Discard if the formula develops an off‑smell, color change, or unusual taste.

infant-formula-enfamil-infant-powder-mad.title: Infant formula, Enfamil Infant, powder, made with bottled water

content.title: About
content.content: Enfamil Infant is a powdered infant formula designed for babies from birth to 12 months. The composition meets the nutritional needs of a growing infant and includes proteins, fats, carbohydrates, vitamins, and minerals. The formula is prepared with bottled water, ensuring consistent purity and mineral content.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Enfamil is one of the most recognized infant nutrition brands, with over 70 years on the market.
The formula contains DHA and ARA – essential fatty acids for brain and eye development.
It is formulated according to WHO guidelines and national pediatric recommendations.
The 335 g package is convenient for travel and small families.
The product has undergone clinical testing confirming its safety and efficacy.

items.title: Supports growth and development
items.content: A balanced mix of proteins, fats, and carbohydrates provides energy and building blocks for tissue growth.

items.title: Brain development
items.content: DHA and ARA help form neural connections and support visual function.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Vitamins A, C, D and zinc aid the body’s defense mechanisms.

items.title: Bone health
items.content: Calcium, phosphorus and vitamin D promote bone and teeth mineralization.

items.title: Easy digestion
items.content: Optimized protein blend and probiotic components improve gastrointestinal tolerance in infants.

items.title: Cow‑milk protein allergy
items.content: Some infants may develop an allergy to cow‑milk proteins; discontinue use and consult a pediatrician if symptoms appear.

items.title: Improper reconstitution
items.content: Too concentrated or too diluted preparations can lead to dehydration or over‑feeding.

items.title: Storage after opening
items.content: Keep the opened container in a dry, cool place and use within 4 weeks.

items.title: Lactose content
items.content: The formula contains a small amount of lactose; infants with lactose intolerance may need a specialized formula.

content.title: How to Prepare
content.content: Mix the specified amount of powder with clean bottled water at room temperature. Stir thoroughly until the mixture is smooth and free of lumps. Use the prepared feed within 2 hours.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened package in a dry, cool place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep it in an airtight container and use within 4 weeks. Discard if the product develops an off‑smell, color change, or unusual taste.

shrimp-shish-kabob-with-vegetables-exclu.title: Shrimp Shish Kabob with Vegetables, No Potatoes

content.title: About
content.content: The shrimp shish kabob with vegetables, no potatoes, is a grilled skewer where large shrimp alternate with chunks of bell pepper, zucchini, onion and cherry tomatoes. All ingredients are marinated in olive oil, lemon juice, garlic and spices, then threaded onto skewers and grilled until lightly charred.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Shrimp are one of the fastest‑growing seafood species, farmed in as little as 3–4 months.
Seafood kebabs are a staple of Mediterranean cuisine, often featuring olive oil and fresh herbs.
Omitting potatoes makes the dish lighter and lowers its glycemic index.
Shrimp get their pink hue from astaxanthin, a powerful antioxidant.
Grilling vegetables quickly retains most of their vitamins compared to prolonged cooking.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Shrimp provide about 20 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Most of the fat in shrimp is polyunsaturated, and the overall fat content is modest.

items.title: Source of iodine and selenium
items.content: These trace minerals are essential for thyroid function and antioxidant defense.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Shrimp contain vitamin B12, niacin and riboflavin, which aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants from vegetables
items.content: Bell peppers and tomatoes are rich in vitamin C and lycopene, boosting immunity.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience severe allergic reactions to shrimp.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Shrimp contain cholesterol, so people with hypercholesterolemia should monitor portion size.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Improper storage or undercooking can allow bacterial growth leading to food poisoning.

items.title: Salt in the marinade
items.content: Excessive salt can raise blood pressure in salt‑sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the kabob hot, straight off the grill. Eat directly from the skewer, cut into bite‑size pieces for salads, rice or couscous dishes, and pair with a light yogurt or tzatziki sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. For longer keeping, freeze in freezer‑safe bags for up to 1 month. Reheat thoroughly to an internal temperature of 75 °C before serving.
